Speaking on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange's investor platform on Tuesday, CATL reaffirmed its target of small-series production of solid-state batteries in 2027, with research and development on fully solid cells continuing. Separately, a sodium-ion energy storage agreement will see up to 3 GWh of capacity deployed in Europe over five years — a letter of intent covering the European energy storage market, according to the company. Indonesia Plant Starts Up Outside China, the joint Indonesian battery plant operated by CATL and Antam has begun production, news agency Antara reported on Thursday. artigo.texto: CATL Returns 19.37 Million Shares to Treasury as Brokerages Rethink the Growth Story Published on 11/01/2026 at 05:52 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has bought back 19.37 million A-shares between September 11 and Wednesday, the battery maker disclosed in a regulatory filing. Wednesday alone accounted for 0.87 million shares, acquired for RMB 199.98 million. The repurchase programme has unfolded against a backdrop of disappointing quarterly figures and mounting competitive pressure that has weighed on the stock. A Quarter That Missed on Both Lines For the third quarter of 2026, CATL reported an unaudited net profit of RMB 21.2 billion, up 14.5% year on year. Revenue climbed 58.6% to RMB 165.2 billion. Neither figure cleared what analysts had pencilled in — consensus had pointed to profit growth of 41.2%. Reuters described the earnings expansion as the weakest in nearly two years, pointing to fiercer competition in batteries and slower growth in Chinese car sales. The shortfall triggered a sharp slide in the share price, with the disappointing results, intensifying battery-market rivalry and softer vehicle demand all cited as triggers. By Friday the stock had recovered some ground, adding 1.7%. Morgan Stanley Steps Back, UOB Trims Its Numbers Morgan Stanley downgraded CATL's H-shares to "In-Line" on Tuesday, according to media reports, and cut its price target by 44.7% to HK$390. UOB Kay Hian had moved two days earlier, on October 22, keeping its buy recommendation on the A-shares but lowering its target to RMB470.00 from RMB585.00. The Singapore-based house also trimmed its net profit forecasts for 2026 through 2028, by 5%, 10% and 16% respectively, expecting CATL to absorb part of higher taxes. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Swapping Batteries, Not Chemistries While the analysts were marking down their models, CATL pressed ahead on the product front. Reuters reported on October 21 that the company unveiled its Tianxing II battery platform, with plans for 900 battery-swap stations for heavy trucks across China by year-end and 2,000 by 2027. The passenger-car side is expanding through partnerships: on October 22, CATL reportedly agreed with Beijing Automotive Group to develop a swap system serving one million vehicles, with BAIC contributing compatible models to the Choco-Swap network and supporting station roll-out through its dealerships. On the technology roadmap, CATL told investors on Tuesday that work on all-solid-state batteries remains on schedule, with small-series production targeted for 2027. O fluxo de caixa do trimestre de julho, que ficou abaixo da metade da estimativa do mercado, diz mais sobre o custo desse alcance. As ações caíram 1,17% em 28 de outubro e 4,22% para $204,64 em 30 de outubro, a primeira sessão após o relatório da Nscale. Naquele dia também ocorreu a queda de 28,58% da Intel e os resultados da Amazon, que enviaram o Philadelphia Semiconductor Index para baixo 7,22%, então a notícia da Nscale não pode ser separada da venda em massa. Uma Investigação Sobre Alocações, uma Garantia para a Anthropic A questão mais incisiva no relatório da Reuters está dentro de uma investigação mais ampla sobre conduta que começou sob o presidente Joe Biden. The cuts come as CATL pushes into battery swapping, energy storage and solid-state cells — expansion that broadens its business but does not yet offer a quick fix for earnings pressure in its core cell operations. UOB Kay Hian reaffirmed its buy rating, citing a quarterly profit that fell short of expectations. Its target for the A-shares dropped sharply, from RMB 585 to RMB 343, though the buy recommendation stands for that share class. Morgan Stanley had already moved on Monday, downgrading the H-shares from "Overweight" to "Equal-weight" and cutting the related target from HK$705 to HK$390. For the A-shares, Morgan Stanley lowered its mark from RMB 500 to RMB 335 while holding its buy call — meaning it changed the rating only on the H-share line, unlike UOB Kay Hian. New Markets, Familiar Rivals The strategic logic behind CATL's diversification is straightforward: with price wars raging and tax rules shifting, battery swapping and storage are meant to open additional revenue streams. The catch, according to Lucas Zhang Liutong, director of WaterRock Energy Economics, is that both fields are already fiercely contested. Nio is firmly entrenched in battery swapping, while BYD holds a strong position in energy storage. CATL is therefore moving into occupied territory rather than empty space. For investors, that is the central limitation of the growth story. New revenue lines can widen the business, but they are not an automatic short-term substitute for profits squeezed in the cell business. Analysts consider it unlikely that swapping and storage will fully offset those pressures anytime soon. The real question is not whether CATL can open new markets, but how fast they can contribute meaningfully to the bottom line. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? A Storage Launch Without a Price Tag CATL took a concrete step in storage on Thursday, unveiling TENER+ in Melbourne. The system offers 9 MWh of storage capacity and is designed for a 25-year service life. Those specs describe technical ambition, not commercial traction: CATL disclosed no price, no delivery date and no order at the presentation. What the launch proves is an expanded product lineup — not that the investment will quickly translate into extra profit against intense competition. Solid-state cells run on a longer clock. Media reports say CATL raised prototype capacity from 10 to 20 Ah, but the cells remain in testing and are not approved for sale. Pilot production in small volumes is planned for 2027, with mass production expected around 2030. That gives investors a clear timeline: swapping and storage are meant to generate new revenue, while solid-state technology stays a longer-term prospect. Indonesia Plant Starts Up as Deals Pile In On the operational front, the news agency Antara reported Thursday that the joint Indonesian battery plant of CATL and Antam has begun production. Indonesia's coordinating minister said President Prabowo is expected to inaugurate the facility soon. The same day, CATL and Dongfeng Motor reportedly signed a strategic cooperation agreement to develop technologies and systems for ultra-fast charging and battery swapping. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. A separate company statement outlined a five-year plan to deploy sodium-ion energy storage systems with up to 3 GWh of capacity in Europe — an arrangement CATL described as a letter of intent, covering the European storage market. Taken together, the flurry of announcements shows a company broadening its footprint on several fronts at once. artigo.texto: CATL's Buyback Tally Reaches 19.37 Million Shares as Quarterly Profit Growth Disappoints Published on 11/01/2026 at 13:21 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has now repurchased a total of 19.37 million A-shares for RMB 5.31 billion, according to a mandatory disclosure filed with the Hong Kong exchange on Wednesday. The buyback programme has been running since 11 September, and the company added another 233,800 shares on Thursday for RMB 53.6726 million — a fresh repurchase notice that landed just after quarterly results had weighed on its Hong Kong-listed stock. The earnings picture those buybacks are cushioning was never going to be pretty. Third-quarter 2026 net profit, reported on 20 October, rose 14.5% to RMB 21.2 billion, falling well short of what analysts had pencilled in. Consensus had pointed to a 41.2% increase, Reuters noted, making the actual figure the weakest growth in nearly two years. Revenue growth also trailed forecasts. Margin Pressure Behind the Miss Several forces combined to squeeze profitability. Reuters pointed to fiercer competition in the battery market and slower growth in Chinese vehicle sales. A lower gross margin, an unfavourable product mix and higher tax costs added to the concern about earnings quality. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Battery Swapping Network Widens Even as the numbers landed, CATL kept building out its swapping business. On 22 October the company agreed with Beijing Automotive Group (BAIC) to develop a system covering one million vehicles. BAIC is expected to bring compatible models into CATL's Choco-Swap network and to use its dealer network to help roll out swap stations. Three days earlier, on 19 October, CATL and its battery-swapping unit Chocolate Swap formed a strategic partnership with Yinwang/Newcool, Huawei's automotive arm, aimed at linking Huawei's intelligent driving systems with CATL's swapping ecosystem. Heavy-Duty Offering Takes Shape For heavy commercial vehicles, CATL unveiled a range-extender battery and a revised QIJI battery-swap solution on 20 October. The concept pairs a swappable main battery with an additional range-extending unit, and the company said it will continue expanding its swapping network. artigo.texto: Sam Altman diz ser “terrível” ter muita memória RAM em computadores pessoais em vez de data centers Declaração ocorre em meio a uma escassez global de memória RAM, resultado do aumento da demanda por chips em diferentes setores da tecnologia, especialmente com a expansão dos data centers voltados à inteligência artificial O CEO da OpenAI, Sam Altman, afirmou ser “terrível” ter muita memória RAM em computadores pessoais em vez de data centers. Segundo o The Verge, durante sua participação no podcast Cheeky Pint, divulgado nesta semana, o executivo foi questionado sobre a escassez de componentes na cadeia de suprimentos, como a atual falta de memória RAM. “Muitas pessoas querem fazer inferência local. E, de alguma forma, elas presumem que o problema está resolvido agora porque teremos modelos de código aberto, poderemos executá-los em nossos computadores e, assim, não precisaremos de todas aquelas coisas nos data centers", disse. "Mas, do ponto de vista de alocação global, na verdade, é bastante terrível que todo mundo tenha uma boa quantidade do estoque limitado de DRAM [tipo mais comum de memória RAM] do mundo em seu próprio computador, sendo usada 5% do tempo", afirmou Altman. "Você quer a máxima utilização na nuvem se está tentando lidar com esse ambiente de oferta muito restrita. E, de alguma forma, a intuição de todos — de muitas pessoas — é o contrário disso", complementou. A declaração ocorre em meio à escassez global de memória RAM, em um cenário de forte disputa por esses componentes. Segundo o The Verge, fabricantes como Samsung e SK Hynix têm contratos de longo prazo com empresas que operam serviços de computação em nuvem, responsáveis por grandes data centers. Projetos como o Stargate, da OpenAI, também reservaram grande parte da produção mundial de RAM para os próximos anos. A forte demanda das empresas de tecnologia por chips para abastecer seus data centers aumenta a disputa por componentes que também são utilizados em computadores e celulares. Com a oferta limitada, essa concorrência pressiona os preços da memória e pode encarecer os produtos eletrônicos.

artigo.texto: The Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC) has officially notified the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (Grid Interactive Distributed Renewable Energy Sources) Regulations, 2026, introducing a comprehensive framework for grid-connected distributed renewable energy systems across the state. Issued under Notification No. 11 of 2026, the new regulations replace the Net Metering Rooftop Solar PV Grid Interactive Systems Regulations, 2016, and establish updated provisions for residential, commercial and industrial consumers adopting distributed renewable energy sources (DRES). The regulations introduce five metering mechanisms: Net Metering, Net Billing, Gross Metering, Group Net Metering and Virtual Net Metering. Under Net Metering and Net Billing, consumers can install systems with capacities ranging from 1 kW AC to 1,000 kW AC or 1,250 kWp DC. Gross Metering systems can have capacities between 6 kW AC and 4,000 kW AC. Group Net Metering allows consumers to share generated electricity across multiple connections belonging to the same entity and consumer category, with a maximum capacity of 1,000 kW AC. Virtual Net Metering provides another option for collective renewable energy adoption, enabling energy sharing across different locations within the jurisdiction of the same distribution licensee. Systems under this arrangement can range from 10 kW AC to 4,000 kW AC, allowing multiple consumers to benefit from renewable electricity generated at a common location. To address grid stability and manage additional renewable energy generation, GERC has introduced mandatory Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) integration requirements for certain consumers. Prosumers with contract demand exceeding 100 kW who intend to install DRES capacity beyond their sanctioned demand must incorporate battery storage. The storage system must support at least two hours of charging and discharging per day for a minimum of 50% of the excess DRES capacity. The regulations also establish different energy settlement mechanisms for residential and non-residential consumers. Residential prosumers under Net Metering will receive 100% adjustment of exported electricity against their grid consumption without banking charges. Any annual surplus energy remaining after adjustment will be purchased by distribution companies at ₹2.25 per kWh. For non-residential consumers, energy adjustment is limited to 30% of total imported electricity during each billing cycle and is subject to applicable banking charges. Any excess electricity injected beyond the permitted adjustment will be treated as lapsed energy. GERC has also prescribed technical and safety requirements for grid-connected systems. All installations must comply with Central Electricity Authority (CEA) standards and the Gujarat Electricity Grid Code. Mandatory anti-islanding protection and automatic isolation devices will ensure safe grid operation. Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) meters with RS-485 ports or advanced communication capabilities will also be required for monitoring electricity flows. Monitoring requirements will depend on project capacity. Systems exceeding 1 MW must install Remote Terminal Units (RTUs), while installations below 1 MW will require SIM-based remote monitoring systems. For implementation, distribution licensees must establish dedicated online portals to manage consumer registrations, applications, processing and approvals within specified timelines. Connectivity charges will range from ₹1,500 for smaller 1–6 kW systems to ₹50,000 for larger installations of up to 4 MW. Additionally, consumers will retain 100% of the carbon credit benefits generated through their systems, while electricity produced under the framework will contribute towards DISCOMs’ Renewable Purchase Obligations (RPO). With the introduction of these regulations, Gujarat has established updated provisions for distributed renewable energy generation, electricity sharing, battery storage integration and grid connectivity across different consumer categories. artigo.texto: CATL Pairs Australian Storage Debut With Sodium-Ion and Swap Push as Margins Face Scrutiny Published on 11/01/2026 at 23:30 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL used the All Energy Australia stage in Melbourne to give its TENER+ energy storage system its global premiere on Thursday, unveiling a unit rated at 9 MWh. Alongside the launch, media reports said the company signed letters of intent with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and UNSW Sydney aimed at backing large-scale battery storage projects across Australia. The Australian showcase is only one strand of a broader push. At the start of November, CATL moved to deepen its bet on energy storage and battery swapping, creating a storage subsidiary with planned registered capital of RMB 5 billion. The vehicle's business plan also takes in AI software. A sodium-ion venture with Intilion, sized at 3 GWh, rounds out the announcements. Those figures describe how the subsidiary will be funded, not the revenue or profit it will generate — a distinction worth keeping in mind when weighing the expansion. Crowded Ground WaterRock Energy Economics reckons competition in the targeted segments is already fierce. In storage, CATL runs into BYD; in battery swapping, Nio stands in the way. The expansion, in other words, does not lead into unoccupied territory. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? Carmakers, meanwhile, are lining up alternative cell suppliers. Li Auto took a RMB 2.65 billion stake in Sunwoda Power in September and holds 8.32% of the company. Xiaomi also bought in. The two automakers run a joint battery venture, and the latest-generation Li Auto L8 uses Sunwoda cells exclusively. Such moves matter to CATL because they strengthen rival supply relationships. Back in 2023, the company offered selected automakers lithium carbonate at RMB 200,000 per tonne, provided they sourced roughly 80% of their battery needs from CATL over three years. The Sunwoda investments show that carmakers are charting their own courses alongside — or instead of — such long-term commitments, raising the value to CATL of sales channels beyond its established customer base. Technology Pipeline Solid-state batteries remain a priority. CATL told investors on Tuesday that it will keep funding the technology, with small-series production targeted for 2027. On swapping, the company agreed on 22 October to deepen cooperation with the BAIC Group. According to media reports, the signed accord covers adapting several BAIC brands to CATL's swap system, with the partners also planning to build out the associated network. There was a legal reprieve in Hungary as well. A court on Friday dismissed a lawsuit brought by residents against the Debrecen battery plant, Reuters reported, on the grounds that the plaintiffs lost standing after the permitting documents were revised. The court also found no regulatory breaches in the approval process, according to the report. The ruling removes a legal burden less than a month after trial production began. CATL at a turning point? This analysis reveals what investors need to know now. Earnings Lag Revenue Third-quarter 2026 figures showed revenue of RMB 165.22 billion, up 58.6% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders came in at RMB 21.25 billion, a gain of 14.5% — meaning earnings growth trailed the top line. Brokers have taken note. Morgan Stanley has flagged pressure from price competition, and Nomura cut its CATL profit forecasts for 2026–2028 in October by as much as 10.2%. The new business lines thus answer economic pressure without yet proving it has been overcome. Storage and swapping widen CATL's footprint, but whether that translates into profitable growth depends on how the company holds its own against entrenched rivals. For investors, the gap between announced expansion and hard earnings contributions is where the real test lies. Ad CATL Stock: New Analysis - 1 November Fresh CATL information released. artigo.texto: ABC 6 asks U.S. Senator Jon Husted about the economy, data centers, and Trump's comments WSYX (Columbus, Ohio) — There's that old political adage: "As Ohio goes, so goes the nation." For the 2026 midterms, that saying could apply to which party controls the U.S. Senate. The race between incumbent Republican U.S. Senator Jon Husted and Democrat Sherrod Brown has gained increased national attention, including visits from President Trump and President Obama in recent weeks to rally support for their party's candidate. ABC 6 anchor Mike McCarthy spoke one-on-one with both Husted and Brown about the major issues in this race. The transcript of the conversation with Husted is below. Brown's interview can be found here. The Economy What's one thing you can point to in your two years in the Senate to say, 'Your life is better because I did, X? What is that? Husted: The Working Families Tax Cut Plan. We cut taxes on tips, overtime, and social security so people could keep more of what they earn to spend and save on their priorities. That's thousands and thousands of dollars more in the pockets of every working family in the state, and it included a $2,200 per child tax credit. So, if you're a family of four or two children, that's $4,400 in your pocket that you wouldn't have had otherwise. That helps people make ends meet by giving them more of what they've earned to spend on their priorities. Republicans have control of the Senate, of the House, of the White House. The overall economy right now obviously is a major concern for so many Ohioans. The latest jobs report shows that growth is weak, mortgage rates are up, inflation is up 3.7%, driven largely by gas prices. It's rising faster than the average hourly earnings for Ohioans, how do you explain that? Husted: Well, I think that your question only asks, only explains half the story. We also in Ohio have the most jobs in the history of our state. We also have the lowest unemployment rate in Ohio, 3.3%. The last time we had a Democrat governor of the state, the unemployment rate was 9%. Now it's 3.3%. And the poverty rate, the lowest in American history right now. And what we've done, we've helped people. We've created more jobs. Wages are rising. We've let people keep more of their money, but we still haven't fought the inflation dragon to the ground, which is what we need to do. It started under Joe Biden and Sherrod Brown. It was at 9%. Gas prices were at $5. They've come down. We need to do more. It's not enough. Groceries are still high. Gas prices are still higher. Electricity's still too high. But I've been fighting on all those fronts, and Sherrod Brown is literally the cause for a lot of it. He voted to give the EPA the ability to shut down power plants. We lost 23 power plants during the Biden and Obama administrations, which Ohio used to be a net electricity exporter. Now it's a net electricity importer. And that's why we have higher prices by and large because we don't have the supply to meet the demand. 90 refineries were closed with the regulations that he voted for, which helped restrict the supply of gasoline production, which is also a factor. You flip those things around, you get those fixed, we have the supply to meet the demand and we can drive down those prices. But yeah, it's not enough. There's still more work that needs to be done. So for folks who, and I understand there are positives going on in the economy, so thank you for pointing that out... Husted: Well, and by the way, let me also point out the fact. The reason that interest rates are growing higher and higher is largely because of $40 trillion in national debt. $34 trillion of it, Sherrod Brown is responsible for. That happened on his watch. And so when you have this debt, people demand higher prices to buy the bonds to finance government. And that drives up interest rates on consumers. And so his failed policies literally are at the ground floor of a lot of these problems. Respectfully though, the latest budget added to the deficit in D.C. Husted: It did not. It actually, it actually reduced the deficit, if you look at the Congressional Budget Office review. It, well, it reduced the rate of the deficit growth. There's no doubt that we spend way too much money though. There is a deficit. It needs to go down. I've been there for 18 months. I can't fix what Sherrod Brown did in 32 years in 18 months, but I'm going to, I'm going to, and that's why people should elect me So if going to back to D.C., if you do win the seat again, what is something you think Congress can be doing next to address these issues that people see when they go to the gas pump, when they got to the grocery store and you're buying a pound of ground beef and it's anywhere from $7 to $9? Husted: The reason that we have these prices is because America has done things to make it more expensive to build everything that we do. You can't lop on all of these radical environmental policies and drive up the cost of producing gasoline and drilling for oil and transporting it. You can't close down power plants. You can't add regulations to farmers and ranchers, and then expect the prices to go down. We have to get rid of those things. We can point at issues here and there, but the bottom line is the problem that we have is if you want to do more 'Made in America 'and you don't want to make things in China, and you want to make it at home, you have to create a regulatory environment where people can actually produce these things for lower prices because if you don't, the price will keep going up. Sherrod Brown built this system. He is the system. 32 years in Washington. He built this failed system. I'm trying to fix it. So what's the next step in trying to undo that and trying to fix it and trying to get help? Husted: One of the things I'm leading is on permitting reform. That's one of the things that we can do to shorten the time. The last time we built a bridge over the Ohio River, it was 13 years to do i

artigo.texto: Principais Estatísticas para a Ação da AMD - Preço Atual: $504.80 - Preço-Alvo (Médio): ~$2,340 - Alvo da Rua: ~$640 - Retorno Total Potencial: ~363% - TIR Anualizada: ~44% / ano O Que Aconteceu? Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) caiu 10,88% para $504,80 em 30 de outubro, dias antes de seu próprio relatório em 3 de novembro. O gatilho foi a Intel (INTC), que revisou sua previsão de receita para o quarto trimestre para $15,0 bilhões a $16,0 bilhões e fechou em queda de 28,58%. No entanto, o mesmo relatório mostrou a receita da Intel com data centers subindo 78%, e os data centers representaram 58% da receita da AMD no segundo trimestre. O Philadelphia Semiconductor Index caiu mais de 7% e a Nvidia 4,22%, com os planos de gastos com IA da Amazon adicionando às preocupações. A AMD caiu mais do que ambas, pois os investidores reavaliaram sua exposição à mesma fraqueza do mercado de PCs. A Intel Vendeu Menos PCs e Servidores Mais Caros "Olhando para frente, vemos a desaceleração do PC continuando pelo menos até a primeira metade do próximo ano", disse o CFO da Intel, David Zinsner. O grupo de clientes e IA física da Intel caiu 5% para $8,1 bilhões, e a Intel espera que a receita com clientes caia mais de 20% em relação ao terceiro trimestre. O lado dos data centers seguiu na direção oposta. A receita com data centers e IA subiu 78% para $7,3 bilhões, e o 10-Q da Intel credita o ganho nos servidores aos preços médios de venda, que subiram 54%. A Intel espera que a divisão cresça em uma porcentagem de dois dígitos médios de forma sequencial no quarto trimestre, embora uma escassez de substratos de embalagem esteja limitando a velocidade com que pode aumentar a produção de servidores. A Receita da AMD Está no Lado que Está Crescendo A receita da AMD com data centers mais do que dobrou para $6,7 bilhões no segundo trimestre, enquanto a receita com clientes subiu 23% para $3,1 bilhões, cerca de 27% das vendas. A Intel também é a principal rival da AMD em servidores, então seu crescimento de 78% fala sobre a força da demanda, não sobre quem está ganhando market share. A queda do mercado de PCs ainda custa algo à AMD. Ela previu que a receita com clientes no terceiro trimestre teria apenas um leve crescimento sequencial, e uma desaceleração do mercado de PCs impulsionada pela memória até 2027 pesaria sobre aproximadamente um quarto de sua receita.

artigo.texto: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Partnership will establish a fully domestic battery supply chain for drones and unmanned aerial vehicles, strengthening the U.S. defense industrial base and eliminating reliance on foreign suppliers. SACRAMENTO, CA, NOVEMBER 2, 2026 – Sparkz, a U.S. battery technology and manufacturing company, today announced plans to establish a dedicated defense battery manufacturing operation in the Midwest in partnership with Global Ordnance. The $100 million project investment is expected to create approximately 355 full-time American jobs including 180 direct manufacturing jobs and 175 spillover jobs and establish a fully domestic battery supply chain supporting drones, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and other critical defense applications. The project represents a significant investment in American manufacturing capacity and national security in alignment with the Trump administration’s implementation of several executive actions, tariffs, and regulatory measures to boost U.S. domestic drone manufacturing and reduce reliance on foreign supply chains, particularly from China. As drones and unmanned systems become increasingly critical to modern defense operations, access to high-performance, domestically manufactured batteries is a strategic priority. Through this partnership, Sparkz and Global Ordnance will bring critical battery manufacturing capabilities to the Midwest, establishing a secure, fully domestic supply chain for the batteries powering next-generation unmanned defense systems. By expanding U.S. production and reducing reliance on overseas manufacturing, particularly from China, the partnership will strengthen the resilience of the American defense industrial base while bringing skilled manufacturing jobs back to the United States. The $100 million project investment is expected to generate approximately 355 full-time jobs, with additional economic benefits through construction, equipment, logistics, and local supplier networks. The partnership reflects a shared commitment to strengthening American manufacturing, securing critical supply chains, and ensuring that the technologies supporting America’s defense capabilities can be produced at home. Additional details regarding the facility’s location, development timeline, and production plans will be announced as the project advances. “This is about rebuilding America’s battery manufacturing capabilities and ensuring our defense industrial base has access to the critical technologies it needs,” said Dr. Sanjiv Malhotra, Founder and CEO of Sparkz. “With a $100 million project investment and approximately 355 American jobs, we are making a substantial commitment to domestic manufacturing. Our partnership with Global Ordnance will help establish a fully domestic battery supply chain for drones and UAVs, reducing our dependence on foreign suppliers and strengthening America’s national security.” Global Ordnance brings defense contracting, regulatory compliance, and systems integration experience to the effort, helping move Sparkz batteries into U.S. and allied unmanned systems programs. The partnership builds on the companies’ collaboration to supply American-made, NDAA-compliant battery solutions for drones and UAVs. “Securing reliable American sources for critical defense components is essential to strengthening our national security,” said Jeff Brunozzi, President of Global Ordnance. “Our partnership with Sparkz will expand the domestic manufacturing base, create hundreds of American jobs, and help ensure that the batteries powering tomorrow’s unmanned defense systems are made in the United States.” About Sparkz Sparkz is an American battery technology and manufacturing company focused on building a vertically integrated domestic lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery supply chain. Sparkz develops and manufactures advanced battery materials, cells, and battery systems for commercial, industrial, energy storage, and defense applications. The company is committed to strengthening American manufacturing, reducing dependence on foreign supply chains, and delivering reliable, domestically produced battery technology. About Global Ordnance Global Ordnance is a veteran-owned defense company headquartered in Tampa, Florida, with offices in three countries, serving U.S. and allied defense markets since 2013. The company supplies U.S.-standard and non-standard ammunition, weapons, energetics, and platforms to military, government, and law enforcement customers worldwide. Global Ordnance also integrates unmanned and counter-unmanned systems, including lethal payloads, working with industry partners to field drone capability for U.S. and allied forces. Built on long-standing relationships with allied governments and a global network of manufacturers, Global Ordnance delivers mission-critical capability where and when its customers need it. PRESS CONTACTS: Michelle Bandur Sparkz VP, Marketing and Communications 279-208-4672 Abby Rodriguez Sparkz VP, Corporate Development 202-743-3831 Margit DeMarco Global Ordnance, Director of Marketing 941-431-7505

artigo.texto: LG CNS has completed a 30-megawatt artificial intelligence data center in Jakarta, Indonesia, marking the first overseas AI data center built by a Korean company for a foreign client, with its entire capacity booked before completion. The facility was commissioned last year by KMG, a joint venture between Indonesia's Sinar Mas Group and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. The project marks LG CNS' entry into overseas AI data center construction for third-party clients. Designed to support next-generation graphics processing units and high-performance computing, the center features a hybrid cooling system combining conventional air cooling with liquid cooling to handle heat generated by AI servers. The initial phase uses air cooling, with liquid cooling to be introduced in a subsequent phase. The facility's power infrastructure can support more than 300 kilowatts per rack, roughly 60 times the capacity of a conventional data center rack. Redundant power systems ensure continued operations in the event of a primary power failure. The project also brings together technologies from LG affiliates under the group's integrated "One LG" strategy, combining LG CNS' data center design, construction and operation capabilities with cooling systems from LG Electronics and batteries from LG Energy Solution. LG CNS is already designing the next phase of the project, which aims to expand the facility's total power capacity to 400 MW. Building on its Indonesian foothold, the company plans to pursue AI data center projects in Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, the Philippines and Japan, as demand for AI computing infrastructure accelerates across Asia. In Korea, LG CNS offers data center colocation, design-build-operate services, modular facilities, GPU-as-a-service and liquid cooling solutions. It also plans to expand into AI factory services by integrating its infrastructure capabilities with AI platforms and applications. "The completion of the Indonesian data center demonstrates our ability to deliver our expertise to overseas clients and compete in global markets," LG CNS CEO Hyun Shin-Gyoon said. "We will use this project as a stepping-stone to expand our AI data center and AI factory businesses across the Asia-Pacific region and beyond." jyoungseon8@heraldcorp.com

artigo.texto: Climate fintech startup Hooxi Partners has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with global carbon market specialist ACT Group to build a one-stop response system for the European Union’s (EU) Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), the company said on the 3rd. The agreement was designed to help South Korean exporters with production and sales subsidiaries in Europe prepare in advance, before mandatory certificate purchases begin in earnest in 2027. The two companies plan to provide an integrated solution covering everything from emissions calculations and verification to certificate cost management. The EU’s CBAM is a so-called “carbon tariff” that charges for carbon emissions generated during the production of imported goods. It has been in effect since January this year for six product categories, including steel and aluminum. Starting in February 2027, importers will be required to purchase and surrender CBAM certificates corresponding to their emissions. Costs tied to carbon emissions are also on a steady upward trajectory. The benchmark certificate price for the third quarter of this year was 82.32 euros per ton, up about 9% from the previous quarter. From 2027, the price-setting period will shift from quarterly to weekly, making careful price-risk management essential for companies. The two companies will divide responsibilities by area of expertise to maximize the efficiency of their support. Hooxi Partners will use its proprietary artificial intelligence (AI) carbon platform, “Carbon AI,” to determine which products are subject to CBAM, collect supplier data, calculate and verify embedded emissions by product, and prepare reporting data. ACT Group will handle EUA-based price-risk management for projected certificate costs, as well as procurement, settlement and custody through its Asia-Pacific entity. “CBAM is no longer simply a reporting obligation; it is a cost issue that exporters and their European subsidiaries must manage together,” said Cho Sung-hoon, co-CEO of Hooxi Partners. “By combining our domestic expertise in emissions calculations and verification with ACT’s execution capabilities in European carbon markets, we will help Korean companies put a complete response system in place before mandatory certificate purchases begin in 2027.”

artigo.texto: Binghamton University is a member of a new national consortium to accelerate the transition of energy storage innovations from discovery to domestic manufacturing. The new Battery Manufacturing (BattMan) Accelerator, led by the U.S. Department of Energy's Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL), will bring together national laboratories, universities, and industry partners to address critical barriers in scaling next-generation battery technologies. Jie Xiao, a Binghamton University alumna, serves as accelerator director. "Breakthroughs in battery science must be matched by our ability to manufacture them at scale," said Jie, the Boeing Martin Professor of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Washington and a Battelle Fellow at PNNL. "This effort brings together the tools, data, and partnerships needed to design manufacturable solutions from the start and accelerate their transition into industry." The BattMan Accelerator will bridge the gap between discovery and manufacturing while establishing comprehensive manufacturing systems with super intelligence that integrate materials development, process design, and production in a seamless manner. Nobel laureate M. Stanley Whittingham, SUNY distinguished professor of chemistry, will serve as the lead investigator from Binghamton. He noted that the accelerator's goals align closely with efforts of the Binghamton-led battery ecosystem that includes New Energy New York and the NSF Energy Storage Engine in Upstate New York. "Incorporating super intelligence into both research and manufacturing allows us to move from trial-and-error to predictive design," Whittngham said. "This capability is key to accelerating innovation while ensuring technologies can be produced reliably and affordably at scale." Whittingham said he expects close interactions between the New York efforts and BattMan. Binghamton is one of five university partners; the others are the University of Washington, University of Alabama, Arizona State University, and the University of Michigan. Argonne and Oak Ridge National Laboratories are also partners. The BattMan Accelerator aligns with the DOE's Genesis vision to integrate super intelligence, materials science, and advanced manufacturing into a coordinated, data-driven innovation ecosystem. The initiative seeks to lower manufacturing costs, speed up development from lab to scale, and boost U.S. leadership in energy storage manufacturing through scientific innovation.

artigo.texto: MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Aeson Power demonstrated the versatility of sodium-ion technology across energy storage and automotive applications at All Energy Australia 2026, held at the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre. At Booth G101, the company presented its latest solutions, highlighting sodium-ion technology's growing role in Australia's energy storage market. Aeson Power's Sodium battery in All-Energy Flexible Sodium-Ion Solutions for Residential Energy Storage A key feature was the APSI2500-based sodium-ion battery system, designed for residential energy storage applications. Combining sodium-ion batteries with Aeson Power's proprietary Ecocase and Ecocab components, the system supports flexible capacity configurations to meet different household energy storage needs. With sodium-ion technology's safety advantages and wide-temperature operating capabilities, the system offers households a flexible energy storage option with safety as a key consideration. Intelligent Energy Storage for Commercial and Industrial Applications Aeson Power also presented the HaloDyne Na 120/119, an all-in-one liquid-cooled sodium-ion energy storage system for commercial and industrial applications. Its sodium-ion chemistry and multi-level fire protection are designed to enhance system safety. With 1C high-rate charging and discharging, the system delivers up to twice the rated power of a comparable 0.5C system with the same battery capacity. This makes it well suited to peak demand management, multi-peak energy arbitrage, and microgrid frequency regulation, where high power output can help reduce the battery capacity needed for specific applications and improve space efficiency. Sodium-Ion Technology for Automotive Starting Applications The exhibition also featured the NaForce sodium-ion starter battery series, demonstrating the growing commercial adoption of sodium-ion technology in the automotive sector. As part of Aeson Power's established product portfolio, NaForce reflects the company's efforts to bring sodium-ion innovation into practical, real-world automotive applications. Together, the three product lines illustrated the versatility of sodium-ion technology, from flexible residential energy storage configurations to integrated commercial energy storage and automotive starting solutions. Through continued product development, Aeson Power aims to deliver reliable performance, safety-conscious design, and flexible integration across evolving energy and automotive markets. Aeson Power's sodium-ion solutions attracted strong interest from visitors at All Energy Australia 2026, prompting engaging discussions with industry professionals throughout the exhibition. About Aeson Power Aeson Power is an Australian pioneer in next-generation battery technology, serving global automotive and energy markets with advanced sodium-ion solutions. Aeson Power designs, develops, and markets high-reliability battery solutions for automotive, energy storage, and more. For more information, visit www.aesonpower.com PR Newswire Asia Ltd. artigo.texto: MELBOURNE, Australia, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LONGi Energy Storage showcased its utility-scale, commercial and industrial (C&I), and microgrid solutions at All Energy Australia 2026, demonstrating its integrated capabilities across diverse energy applications. Under its LONGi ONE strategy, LONGi Energy Storage continues to advance technology innovation and localized services to support Australia's energy transition. LONGi Energy Storage at All Energy Australia 2026 Solutions for Diverse Energy Applications As Australia expands renewable energy deployment, energy storage is increasingly important for grid flexibility, energy cost optimization and reliable power supply. OneMatrix Solution addresses utility-scale applications, including renewable energy projects, standalone grid-side storage and electricity market operations. Featuring flexible modular design and LONGiBank 3.0, it supports 2–8-hour duration and customized system configurations. Cluster-level independent management, AI-powered battery health diagnostics and intelligent O&M help improve operational efficiency and support long-term asset performance. The solution has received TÜV Rheinland certifications under IEC 62619, IEC 63056, and an IEC/EN 60730-1 Annex H report, reinforcing its safety credentials for international markets. Hi-MO One Pro supports C&I applications with flexible 2-24-hour configurations for solar-plus-storage, peak-valley arbitrage, and backup power. Featuring LONGi's proprietary iCCS and liquid-cooling technology, it supports grid-connected and off-grid operation, helping businesses optimize energy costs and enhance power supply security. OneNexus H2 and M5 serve remote areas, mining operations and other locations with limited grid access. By coordinating solar, battery storage and diesel generation, they help increase renewable energy utilization, reduce diesel dependence and strengthen power supply resilience. Project Experience Demonstrates Local Market Value In Strathalbyn, South Australia, the Lunio Energy BESS project was connected to the grid in September 2026. Comprising four LONGiBank 2.0 systems with a total capacity of 5 MW/20 MWh, the project participates in Australia's National Electricity Market (NEM), optimizing charging and discharging in response to electricity demand and market prices. Advancing LONGi ONE Through Localized Services LONGi continues to integrate proprietary technologies, system solutions and intelligent O&M under its LONGi ONE strategy, providing support from solution design and delivery through lifecycle operations. Through its "2830 Plan," LONGi aims to establish 30 comprehensive local service centers worldwide by the end of 2028, strengthening local responsiveness and lifecycle support. With its full-stack capabilities, diverse solution portfolio and expanding local service network, LONGi Energy Storage will continue working with Australian customers and partners to deliver flexible, reliable and sustainable energy solutions. artigo.texto: Graphene batteries have earned a reputation as a promising material for improving battery performance. Its remarkable electrical conductivity, enormous surface area, and ability to distribute heat make it attractive for batteries and supercapacitors. Meanwhile, rare earth elements are better known for powering electric motors, wind turbines, and industrial equipment through their magnetic properties. At first glance, the two have little in common. Graphene is a form of carbon, while rare earths are a group of 17 metallic elements. They perform different functions, and rare earths are not generally necessary ingredients in graphene-enhanced lithium-ion batteries. But researchers are discovering something more interesting than an indirect connection through manufacturing equipment: certain rare earth compounds can work directly with graphene to improve experimental energy-storage electrodes. Studies published in 2025 and 2026 suggest that combining graphene derivatives with rare earth oxides may help address limitations in conductivity, charge storage, and cycling stability. The research is still developing, but it raises an intriguing question: Could two seemingly unrelated materials become partners in next-generation energy storage? Table of Contents Different Materials, Complementary Strengths A conventional lithium-ion battery stores and releases energy through the movement of lithium ions between electrodes. Its performance depends heavily on electrode chemistry, conductivity, ion transport, and thermal stability. A graphene battery can help address some of those challenges. Composed of carbon atoms arranged in a single-atom-thick honeycomb lattice, graphene has excellent electrical conductivity and a large theoretical surface area. In practical energy-storage applications, graphene-related materials can serve as conductive additives, protective coatings, or structural components in composite electrodes. Rare earth compounds offer different advantages. Certain rare earth oxides, particularly cerium oxide (CeO₂), exhibit useful electrochemical properties associated with their ability to participate in oxidation-reduction reactions. These reactions can contribute to charge storage in specially designed electrodes. However, metal oxides can suffer from limited electrical conductivity or other material constraints. This is where graphene becomes interesting. By incorporating rare earth oxide particles into graphene-based structures, researchers can potentially combine the electrochemical activity of the oxide with the electrical and structural advantages of the carbon material. Rather than competing for the same function, the two materials may compensate for each other's weaknesses. Cerium and Graphene: A Partnership Taking Shape One of the clearest examples appeared in a May 2025 study published in the Journal of Colloid and Interface Science. Researchers developed a composite consisting of cerium oxide nanoparticles distributed across graphene oxide nanosheets. They tested the material as a battery-type cathode for a supercapacitor. The distinction matters. A battery-type electrode uses electrochemical reactions that resemble aspects of battery charge storage, but the complete device in this study was a supercapacitor, not a conventional lithium-ion battery. The researchers found that combining redox-active cerium oxide with graphene oxide produced favorable electrochemical behavior, including low ion-diffusion resistance and promising cycling stability. The findings demonstrated how a rare earth compound and a graphene derivative could complement one another within the same electrode. The study, Cerium Oxide Nanoparticles Decorated on Graphene Oxide Nanosheets as Battery-Type Cathode Material for Supercapacitors (opens in a new tab), provides a direct experimental connection between rare earth materials and graphene-based energy storage. More recently, a May 2026 study in Solid State Sciences investigated composites combining multiple rare earth oxides with reduced graphene oxide. Its optimized electrode material achieved a reported specific capacitance of 1,598 farads per gram at a current density of 1 ampere per gram. That result is encouraging, although it describes electrode performance under specified experimental conditions. It cannot be interpreted as the energy-storage capacity of a commercially available battery. Together, these studies suggest that rare earth–graphene combinations deserve further investigation, particularly in supercapacitors and hybrid energy-storage systems. Batteries and Supercapacitors: Where Could the Partnership Matter? Batteries and supercapacitors both store electrical energy, but they excel at different tasks. Lithium-ion batteries generally provide greater energy storage for their size or weight, making them useful when sustained operation matters. Supercapacitors typically charge and discharge much faster and tolerate large numbers of cycles, but store less energy. Researchers are investigating hybrid devices that combine different charge-storage mechanisms to improve the balance between energy density, power delivery, and durability. Graphene-based materials are promising in this field because they can support rapid electron transport and provide accessible surfaces for charge storage. Rare earth oxides could contribute additional electrochemical activity, depending on the particular compound and electrode design. Potential applications include regenerative braking, industrial power systems, and equipment requiring rapid bursts of electricity. However, the technology faces several hurdles before commercial adoption. Researchers must demonstrate that promising electrode-level performance translates into complete, practical devices. They must also address manufacturing costs, material consistency, long-term stability, and scalability. artigo.texto: From January to September this year, the volume of batteries used in electric, plug-in hybrid, and hybrid vehicles registered globally reached 994.5 GWh, a 19.7% increase compared to the same period last year. While the combined market share of seven Chinese companies rose to 73.0%, the combined share of the three domestic firms—LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On—fell to 12.6%. Battery usage at 994.5 GWh According to SNE Research, an energy market research firm, on the 2nd, global battery usage from January to September 2026 was recorded at 994.5 GWh. The data covers batteries installed in pure electric vehicles (EVs) as well as plug-in hybrid vehicles (PHEVs) and hybrid vehicles (HEVs). Usage in September alone reached 145.1 GWh, setting a monthly record. However, the growth rate compared to the same month last year was 15.8%, down from 18.3% in August, indicating a slight slowdown in monthly growth momentum. Chinese firms' market share reaches 73% The combined market share of seven Chinese battery manufacturers rose to 73.0%, up 3.5 percentage points from a year ago. Conversely, the combined share of the three Korean companies—LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI, and SK On—fell to 12.6%, a decrease of 4.1 percentage points. By company, China's CATL maintained the top spot with 81.9 GWh in usage. This represents a 24.9% increase from the same period last year, and its market share expanded from 37.5% to 39.1%, driven by increased supply to overseas automakers. BYD ranked second with 150.9 GWh. Its usage grew by 7.4%, but because this fell short of the overall market growth rate, its market share dipped from 16.9% to 15.2%. The combined market share of CATL and BYD reached approximately 54%.

artigo.texto: LG CNS has secured lease agreements for 100% of its artificial intelligence (AI) data center capacity in Indonesia ahead of completion. Meanwhile, the company said it would invest gradually in its graphics processing unit (GPU) services business after assessing demand and commercial viability. During its third-quarter earnings conference call on Oct. 30, LG CNS announced that its AI data center in Jakarta, Indonesia, is scheduled for completion in early November. The company added that the facility has already secured tenants for its entire capacity. “We secured customers to lease the entire facility before completion, establishing a stable revenue base from the start of operations,” said Yoo Ki-woong, vice president of LG CNS’ AI and Cloud Business Division, during the conference call. He explained that the company is pursuing additional data center construction projects in Indonesia and exploring expansion into North America and Europe. The Indonesian data center is LG CNS’ first overseas AI data center construction project. In 2024, the company signed a data center consulting and design contract with local operator KMG. It subsequently secured a 100 billion won infrastructure construction contract in August 2025. KMG is a joint venture established by Indonesia’s Sinar Mas Group and Korea Investment Real Asset Management. LG CNS participated in the project through LG Sinar Mas Technology Solutions, its joint venture with Sinar Mas Group. The first-phase data center has 11 above-ground floors, a total floor area of 46,281 square meters and a power intake capacity of 30 megawatts (MW). It can accommodate more than 100,000 servers. Project owner KMG plans to expand total power intake capacity to 220 MW. In North America and Europe, LG CNS plans to focus on prefabricated modular data centers. “We are pursuing business cooperation through our U.S. subsidiary and local partners,” Yoo said. “We plan to enter the market using modular data center technology designed to support Nvidia’s next-generation AI platform, Vera Rubin.” According to the company, the modular approach reduces on-site construction work compared with conventional methods and allows facilities to be expanded in stages according to customer demand. However, LG CNS intends to manage investment risks in its GPU services business separately from its broader AI infrastructure expansion. LG CNS chief financial officer (CFO) Song Kwang-ryun expressed a positive view of the medium- to long-term growth potential of GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) during the conference call. He said the company is reviewing business opportunities involving LG Group affiliates and external enterprises but must consider the substantial upfront investment costs and rapid pace of technological change. “We will proceed cautiously, focusing on projects with established commercial viability,” Song said of future investments. LG CNS previously decided at a Sept. 11 board meeting to invest 381.4 billion won in GPUs and infrastructure equipment, including Nvidia’s Vera Rubin. The equipment acquisition is scheduled for June 30, 2027. The company appears to intend to determine the scale of future GPUaaS investments based on actual demand and profitability, separately from the GPU investment already approved. GPUs require substantial upfront capital, and rapid equipment replacement cycles mean customer acquisition and utilization rates can significantly affect investment returns. Meanwhile, AI and cloud revenue reached 961.5 billion won in the third quarter, accounting for 57.8% of LG CNS’ total revenue of 1.6643 trillion won.

artigo.texto: Dongwha Electrolyte, a subsidiary of Dongwha Enterprise, will participate in a 130 billion won next-generation battery research project. The company will focus on developing electrolytes for sodium-ion batteries and establishing quality standards for the technology. Dongwha Electrolyte said November 3 that it would join the Market-Leading Next-Generation Battery Innovation Strategy Research Group (K-BIC). It is the only electrolyte manufacturer among the participating organizations. K-BIC is part of the Global TOP Strategic Research Group support program, jointly promoted by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the National Research Council of Science and Technology. The project has a total budget of 130 billion won and aims to secure fundamental technologies for next-generation batteries and accelerate their commercialization. Dongwha Electrolyte will participate in the second phase of the research project titled "Development of Ultra-Low-Cost, Long-Life Non-Lithium Batteries," led by the Korea Institute of Energy Research. The project aims to develop low-cost sodium-ion batteries priced at less than $50 per kilowatt-hour (kWh). The company will be responsible for electrolyte manufacturing and supply, defining key quality characteristics and establishing quality standards. The research group will expand its scope beyond conventional materials development to include cell development, the expansion of mass-production processes and safety validation. Kim Jong-hoon, CEO of Dongwha Electrolyte, said, "We will secure sodium-ion battery materials technologies that address the needs of the energy storage system (ESS) industry and expand our portfolio of next-generation products."

artigo.texto: 'KODEX All Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus' ETF Surpasses KRW 300 Billion in Net Assets Nearly KRW 200 billion increase over the past month Investing across the ESS value chain and all-solid-state batteries Three-month return of 22.2%, the highest among peers Samsung Asset Management said on November 3 that its KODEX All Solid State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus exchange-traded fund (ETF) surpassed KRW 300 billion in net assets, reaching KRW 334.2 billion. Since the product was listed on June 23, cumulative net purchases by individual investors have reached KRW 76.7 billion, including KRW 24.4 billion in net purchases over the past month alone. As a result, net assets increased by nearly KRW 200 billion over the past month, the largest increase among domestic equity ETFs. The fund is believed to have continued attracting inflows on the back of a clear recovery in earnings at its key holdings and the medium- to long-term growth prospects of the ESS and all-solid-state battery industries. It also posted a 22.2% return over the past three months, ranking first among ETFs in similar categories, including secondary batteries and all-solid-state batteries. The ETF invests about 50% of its assets in two leading domestic battery cell makers, Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution. Strong third-quarter results recently announced by both companies, along with their success in securing global orders, have further enhanced their investment appeal. Samsung SDI returned to profitability in the third quarter of this year, posting revenue of KRW 4.6856 trillion and operating profit of KRW 407.8 billion, driven by increased sales of ESS and battery backup units (BBUs) for AI data centers. LG Energy Solution also reported a marked improvement in results, with preliminary third-quarter revenue of KRW 9.6434 trillion, up 59.0%, and operating profit of KRW 756 billion, up 25.7%. The remaining approximately 50% of the portfolio is invested across ESS component and equipment makers and all-solid-state battery materials companies, aiming to capture supply-chain spillover benefits from increased orders for major cell makers. It holds ESS value-chain companies such as Sangsin EDP, HanJung NCS, Seojin System, and SFA Nexel, which are positioned to benefit from expanded mass production and capital investment. In the all-solid-state battery sector, it also holds key materials companies including ISU Specialty Chemical, Daejoo Electronic Materials, LOTTE Energy Materials, POSCO Future M, and L&F. The Market-Leading Next-Generation Secondary Battery Innovation Strategic Research Group is a battery-sector initiative under the Global TOP Strategic Research Group Support Program, bringing together leading industry, academic, research, and government organizations in Korea’s battery sector. The project has a total budget of KRW 130 billion and aims to overcome technological challenges in next-generation secondary batteries, secure core technologies, and establish an R&D collaboration platform. Dongwha Electrolyte is currently the only electrolyte company among the participating research institutions. Dongwha Electrolyte will join Phase 2 of the “Development of Ultra-Low-Cost, Long-Life Non-Lithium Secondary Batteries,” which aims to develop sodium-ion batteries (SIBs), considered a next-generation energy storage system (ESS) battery. The research will expand beyond the development of existing materials to cover areas that take demonstration into account, including cell development, commercialization process scale-up, and safety assurance. Dongwha Electrolyte will focus on manufacturing and supplying standard electrolytes, defining key electrolyte quality characteristics, and establishing electrolyte quality standards. The Korea Institute of Energy Research will lead the project. artigo.texto: CATL Lays Out Solid-State Timetable as Australian Storage Launch and Hungary Court Win Broaden Its Base Published on 11/01/2026 at 18:40 | Editorial boerse-global.de CATL has told investors it expects to turn out fully solid-state batteries in small production runs by 2027, a disclosure made on the interactive platform of the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Tuesday. The company was careful to frame the target as small-series output rather than mass manufacturing, and stressed that it remains committed to research and development in the technology. The solid-state roadmap sits alongside an unusually busy stretch of partnership announcements. On 19 October, CATL agreed with Yinwang Intelligent Technologies and its battery-swapping subsidiary to build an intelligent system for exchanging electric-vehicle batteries. Three days later, on 22 October, it signed a deeper cooperation agreement with Beijing Automotive Group covering a swap system that, according to The Business Times, is designed to serve one million vehicles. BAIC will bring compatible models into CATL's Choco-Swap network, and its dealer network will help roll out the swapping stations. Heavy Trucks Get Their Own Platform Commercial vehicles are a separate front. CATL unveiled its Tianxing II battery platform for heavy trucks on 20 October; the company says its Qiji system can swap a truck battery in roughly five minutes. The build-out targets are ambitious: 900 heavy-truck swap stations in China by the end of 2026, 2,000 by 2027, and 10,000 over the longer term. A further agreement on 21 October with Shaanxi Transportation Holding Group covers swap infrastructure for heavy trucks as well as solar installations with storage and charging equipment along motorways, plus services spanning the battery life cycle and recycling. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying CATL? TENER+ Makes Its Debut in Australia Away from swapping, CATL introduced its TENER+ energy storage system, with 9 MWh of capacity, globally on Thursday at All Energy Australia. Media reports said the company also signed letters of intent at the show with Hitachi Energy, EPEC Group and UNSW Sydney to support large battery storage projects in Australia. In Hungary, a court on Friday dismissed a lawsuit brought by residents against the Debrecen battery plant, according to Reuters. The residents were no longer entitled to sue after the permitting documents were revised, and the court found no procedural irregularities in the approval process. The ruling removes a legal burden less than a month after trial production began. Revenue Outpaces Earnings The quarter's figures show top-line momentum running well ahead of the bottom line. Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 came in at RMB 165.22 billion, up 58.6% year on year. Net profit attributable to shareholders reached RMB 21.25 billion, a gain of 14.5% — leaving profit growth trailing revenue growth by a wide margin. artigo.texto: Core Scientific currently faces pending air quality enforcement from the state for alleged violations including excessive emissions while temporarily running backup generators at its AI data center in Denton. The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality alerted Core Scientific on July 24 to a notice of enforcement that stemmed from the tech company running eight emergency generators between April and June while resolving manufacturing defects in 93 site transformers, city staff reported to Denton City Council on Friday. If violations are serious enough to warrant action, the TCEQ can enforce compliance and seek penalties through two types of enforcement actions: administrative orders, which are allowed if Core Scientific agrees to TCEQ’s terms and conditions, or referral to the Texas Attorney General’s Office for enforcement through the court and potential civil penalties. Core Scientific didn’t respond to a request for comment by Monday evening. Mayor Pro Tem Nick Stevens asked city staff to look into Core Scientific’s possible violations last week, during the final public hearing for a moratorium that would pause development of new data centers in Denton for 90 days. He reminded the staff that effects on the environment were one of the reasons he pitched the idea of a data center moratorium in June. Stevens alerted the public to TCEQ’s notice of enforcement in a social media post Friday, writing that Core Scientific had “allegedly exceeded their maximum emission rates, exceeded hour limits on emergency generators, failed to obtain a federal permit required for major sources of air pollution and failed to maintain records demonstrating their compliance.” Denton has two data centers previously approved by the council. Core Scientific’s center is nearing full buildout with a contract for up to 394 megawatts of power, while Qumulus’ modular AI data center, which hasn’t broken ground yet, has contracted up to 20 megawatts of power. “If [Core Scientific’s] emissions are five times higher than what the permit allows — or I think one of the things that was said in the staff report was that they haven’t been even keeping files of some of these errors — I mean, there’s a huge environmental hazard,” Stevens told the Denton Record-Chronicle on Monday. “I certainly don’t want residents to feel gaslit, where they’ve been coming to the dais for years saying this is an environmental hazard and repeatedly told it’s not. “Hopefully, it puts that conspiracy theory to bed.” In late June, the TCEQ conducted an investigation of two Core Scientific data center sites in Denton to evaluate compliance with air quality regulations. The company had obtained authorization to construct and operate emergency generators, as well as the associated fuel storage, in February 2025 and subsequently modified emission rates. Matthew Klentzman, a senior construction project manager for Core Scientific, told the TCEQ in late April that the company had identified “a systemic internal manufacturing defect affecting ninety-three transformers,” according to the July 22 TCEQ investigation report. “The defect was determined to be a credible risk of additional transformer failures which could result in loss of data center operations, equipment damage and broader system instability,” Luke Jones, an environmental investigator for TCEQ, wrote in the July 22 report. “Therefore, Core Scientific determined it would be necessary to operate four of their emergency generators on a temporary basis until corrective actions could be taken.” In April, Jones reported that he requested records via email and made follow-up requests on May 7, May 18 and May 26, when the records were finally provided. Jones reviewed the records and determined that not all of the requested information had been provided, noting that it appeared four additional emergency generators had been used to provide power during what the TCEQ called a non-emergency event between April 9 and June 23. During this period of operation, the TCEQ reported that the eight generators resulted in total emissions of 384.13 tons of nitrogen oxides, 50.10 tons of carbon monoxide and 2.51 tons of particulate matter. TCEQ reported that these amounts exceeded the certified limits of 24.9 tons per year of nitrogen oxides, 8.17 tons per year of carbon monoxide and 0.85 tons per year of particulate matter for all emergency generators at the site. As the TCEQ indicated, Denton County is in the Dallas-Forth Worth ozone non-attainment area, which is classified as severe for ozone levels. TCEQ also indicated that Core Scientific operated eight of its emergency generators for non-emergency use for more than the 100 hours per year allowed. TCEQ said four generators were running between 1,352 and 1,371 hours at one building on the property and four generators were running between 527 and 1,024 hours at another building. In addition, the TCEQ requested records of volatile organic compounds emissions from the storage and handling of diesel fuel during Core Scientific’s operation with the emergency generators between April 9 and June 23, as well as the 12-month period prior to then, “No emissions calculations were provided,” according to the violation. artigo.texto: [Newsworks = Reporter Chae Yoon-jung] LG Energy Solution announced on the 29th that it will hold the 'Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) 2026.' The Battery Innovation Contest (BIC) is LG Energy Solution's flagship global research competition program. By selecting outstanding research projects from universities and research institutes and providing funding, and involving LG Energy Solution’s research team in the research process through ongoing feedback, the program helps commercialize the academic community’s creative ideas. All universities and research institutions, both domestic and international, are eligible to participate, and the application period for this year runs from the 29th of this month to December 6. Support is available through the BIC communication program BRIDGE, and LG Energy Solution selects recipients based on the technical maturity and commercialization potential of the proposed research. Since its inception in 2017, BIC is celebrating its 10th anniversary this year by expanding its research topics to the largest scale ever, further strengthening its role as an industry-academia collaboration platform. It is expected that two-way collaboration between industry and academia will become more active through more specialized topics. The designated research topics cover all areas of future battery technology, from materials to cells, BMS, and AI, including ▲ analytical techniques for cell condition diagnosis and ▲ elucidating mechanisms to enhance safety. The R&D teams of LG Energy Solution's key business units directly selected the topics they wish to collaborate on. Since 2017, more than 50 research projects have received support through the BIC program. Among these, the research topic with proven validity is being expanded and operated as the Frontier Research Laboratory (FRL), a joint research center between LG Energy Solution and leading universities and research institutions at home and abroad. If expanded to FRL, LG Energy Solution will provide additional research funding and deploy its research personnel to support in-depth studies. At last year’s BIC, the company was recognized for its many achievements, including filing a patent related to a physical model that improves BMS computation speed. In 2019, research on long-life all-solid-state batteries that operate at room temperature was published in the world-renowned journal Science by FRL. LG Energy Solution plans to continue supporting communication and project management between industry and academia through BIC’s communication program, BRIDGE, this year. BRIDGE is an integrated, two-way system for academia and industry, designed to reduce unnecessary communication during the research and development process and to enable more efficient communication and convenient project history management. By implementing a structured system, the technology for collaborative projects was protected while minimizing offline work to enhance research efficiency. Prior to this, LG Energy Solution recently signed a strategic memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Energy at its headquarters in Park One, Yeouido, Seoul, to collaborate on ESS projects in Europe and North America. Under this agreement, LG Energy Solution plans to collaborate with Endriggs to supply a total of 2 GWh within the next 24 months, targeting approximately 1.5 GWh in Europe and 0.5 GWh in North America.
